subject: Unplanned GPU pool congestion impacting FrameTech - immediate review
messages:
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@frametech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@frametech.com
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Latency + 5xx errors from our Dedicated pool (important)

Ben / Laura —

We're seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end latency for requests routed to our dedicated pool (customer_id: FT-783). Median generation latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s starting ~02:30 UTC this morning, and we're also observing intermittent 5xx responses (mainly 503 / upstream timeouts). Throughput has dropped ~30% against our reserved capacity. This is impacting our production inference jobs and batch scoring windows.

Attached is a short sample of error lines and request IDs (ft_error_sample.log). We've already switched a subset of traffic to our fallback endpoints, but that increases our cost and adds variability in response semantics. Please advise immediately — we need root cause and ETA for recovery.

Chris Nolan
Head of Platform Engineering, FrameTech
chris.nolan@frametech.com

On a related note: procurement is asking whether this incident will affect our committed SLAs and if credits will be offered. Katie from procurement is CC'd.

Chris — thanks for the sample and flagging this. Really sorry for the impact. I'm escalating immediately.

Immediate steps:
- I'm putting you on a 30-min troubleshooting bridge with our on-call infra (Grace) and engineering (aditya.rao@redwood.ai). Can you join a quick call at 09:45 EST?
- We'll collect expanded diagnostics (KV cache stats, scheduler queue depths, GPU utilization) and push a temporary routing policy if needed.

For procurement: we will document the incident and discuss credits after we confirm root cause and window. I'll own communication and keep you updated every 60 minutes.

Best,

Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Latency + 5xx errors from our Dedicated pool — FT-783 (urgent)

Team — forwarding FrameTech's report. Key points:
- Dedicated pool (FT-783) experiencing median latency spike to ~1.8s and ~30% throughput drop vs reserved baseline.
- Intermittent 503s tied to upstream timeouts. Customer has partial fallback routing in place (raises quality drift).
- Customer is asking about SLA credits; procurement on CC.

Please treat as P1. Grace, can you lead the bridge at 09:45 EST and gather: GPU utilization per node, scheduler backlog, KV-cache hit/miss rates, batch sizes in flight, and any rapid kernel timeouts.

Rishi/Aditya — if this looks like pooling saturation or slow eviction behavior, we may need:
  1) immediate temporary autoscale bump for FT-783 or short-term routing of a % of requests to hosted nodes;
  2) a soft rollback of the recent kernel selector tweak (deployed Friday) if correlated;
  3) quick diagnostic artifact (rt-diagnostics-20261108.tar.gz) created by infra.

I've attached the customer's error sample for context. I'm on the bridge.

— Ben
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency + 5xx errors from our Dedicated pool — FT-783 (diagnostic + mitigation)

Summary from the bridge (quick notes):
- Cause signal: scheduler queue backpressure + uneven batch coalescing after Friday's kernel-selection tweak. A subset of GPUs hit longer kernel latencies under the FT-783 request mix (long tail sequences + high concurrency).
- Evidence: elevated scheduler queue depth, per-GPU kernel run durations increased ~3x on two replica hosts, KV cache eviction spike.

Immediate mitigations applied (now):
1) Reverted kernel-selector change for FT-783 (rollback committed at 09:58 EST).
2) Temporarily increased dedicated pool allocation for FT-783 by +20% (autoscale override until 12:00 EST).
3) Enabled short-term request shedding for low-priority batch jobs to preserve interactive latency.

Next steps (hours):
- Collect and upload rt-diagnostics-20261108.tar.gz (logs + perf counters) to the FrameTech folder.
- Engineering to run a focused perf regression on the Friday tweak and propose a targeted kernel/tensor algorithm change.
- Product to coordinate communication on SLA credit assessment after incident window.

If mitigation holds, we will start a phased rollback of the autoscale override and monitor for recurrence.

-Aditya
Senior Engineering Manager, Infra
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx errors from our Dedicated pool (status update)

Chris / Katie —

Quick update from the triage bridge:
- Root cause appears tied to a kernel-selector change rolled out Friday that interacted poorly with your request distribution (long tails + high concurrency).
- Actions taken: rollback of the change, +20% temporary autoscale to your dedicated pool, and shedding of non-critical batch jobs.
- We are monitoring closely and will provide a full diagnostics bundle once logs are consolidated.

ETA: we expect the immediate window to stabilize within 1–2 hours; we'll confirm when median latency returns to baseline and 5xxs disappear.

About SLA/procurement: we will document the incident and follow the credit matrix in your contract. Laura will coordinate the formal impact assessment and next steps with procurement.

Apologies again for the disruption. If you'd like, we can keep the temporary capacity bump in place through EOD while we finish the regression test. Please reply with your preference.

Ben Carter

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0500
Subject: Follow-up: FT-783 incident summary and exec ask

Team — finalizing the incident summary for FrameTech. Thanks to everyone who mobilized over the weekend. A few notes for record and exec alignment:

- Incident window: 2026-11-08T02:30:00Z — 2026-11-08T13:05:00Z (stabilized after rollback + capacity bump).
- Impact: median latency spike to ~1.8s; throughput deficit ~30% vs reserved baseline; transient 503s affecting ~0.6% of requests during peak.
- Root cause: interaction between recent kernel-selector tweak and FT-783 workload characteristics (concurrency + long-tail sequences).
- Mitigations: rollback, +20% temporary pool allocation, job-shedding for low-priority batches.
- Artifacts: rt-diagnostics-20261108.tar.gz uploaded to FrameTech folder; SLA_summary_FrameTech_Q4_2026.pdf drafted for procurement.

Exec ask: please approve the proposed customer remediation package. Recommendation:
  1) Offer a pro-rated usage credit for the affected window per the contractual credit matrix.
  2) Keep the +20% buffer in place through Friday 2026-11-12 to reduce recurrence risk while regression is validated.
  3) Sponsor a short joint postmortem with FrameTech next week (30–45 min) to review root cause and planned kernel fix.

Ben — please take lead on the customer-facing summary and procurement conversation. Aditya / Rishi — aim to have a regression PR and internal perf notes by 2026-11-12.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
